players.product: NovaLT and Frame 5 gas turbines plus Brush generators for behind-the-meter data-center power (Chart Industries thermal management added July 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 headline results (CEO/CFO): Q4 adjusted EBITDA $1.34 billion, above the midpoint of guidance and up 2% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA margin a record 18.1% (above 18% for the first time); Q4 adjusted EPS $0.78 (GAAP diluted EPS $0.88); total company Q4 orders $7.9 billion, including $4 billion from IET. Full year 2025: record adjusted EBITDA $4.83 billion with margin up 90 basis points to a record 17.4%; adjusted EPS $2.60, up 10% from 2024; record free cash flow of $2.7 billion (57% conversion versus a 45% to 50% target), helped by working capital efficiency and higher customer down payments. OFSE full-year revenue fell 8% to $14.3 billion with EBITDA of $2.62 billion (18.3% margin) amid macro-driven softness.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 adjusted EBITDA $1.34 billion (18.1%); adjusted EPS $0.78; orders $7.9 billion; FY adjusted EBITDA $4.83 billion (17.4%); FY adjusted EPS $2.60; FY free cash flow $2.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: IET segment: Q4 orders of $4 billion, driven mainly by power systems and LNG; record full-year orders of $14.9 billion, above the high end of guidance, for a book-to-bill of 1.1x, with non-LNG equipment approximately 85% of IET orders for the second consecutive year; record IET RPO of $32.4 billion at year-end, the sixth consecutive year of IET RPO growth. Q4 IET revenue $3.81 billion (above the high end of guidance on project execution and timing) and record EBITDA of $761 million (+19% year-over-year), margin up 160 basis points to 20%. Full-year IET revenue rose 10% to $13.4 billion and EBITDA 21% to $2.5 billion, margin up 170 basis points to 18.5% - historical highs for all three. 2025 LNG equipment orders were $2.3 billion, with similar levels of LNG awards expected in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: IET Q4 orders $4 billion; FY orders $14.9 billion (book-to-bill 1.1x); IET RPO $32.4 billion; Q4 IET revenue $3.81 billion, EBITDA $761 million (20%); FY IET revenue $13.4 billion, EBITDA $2.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Power systems orders increased significantly to $2.5 billion in 2025, 'including $1 billion tied to data center applications', reflecting 'accelerating demand and growing customer confidence'. 2025 was a milestone year for NovaLT industrial gas turbines (engineered for distributed and behind-the-meter applications, where Baker Hughes sees its strongest growth): approximately 2 gigawatts of orders across oil and gas, industrial and data center markets. Oil and gas power applications added orders of approximately 3 gigawatts in 2025; in Q&A the CEO also cited orders of 1.3 gigawatts for aeroderivative gas turbines within oil and gas. Capacity (CFO): 'we are on track to double our Nova capacity by the first half of '27', and including those planned additions 'our Nova slots are effectively full through 2028'; the incremental capacity will support the 2 gigawatts of Nova orders booked to backlog during 2025, and any expansion beyond the current doubling would follow a disciplined supply-demand and return assessment - 'our current and planned NovaLT capacity is fully committed through '28, but we are prepared to respond quickly if market conditions and customer demand warranted.'
quarterly_data.figure: power systems orders $2.5 billion (2025), including $1 billion data center; NovaLT approximately 2 gigawatts of orders; Nova capacity doubling by the first half of '27, slots effectively full through 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 power awards: 'a large slot reservation agreement for approximately 1 gigawatt of NovaLT capacity to support data center applications, which we expect to convert into a firm order in 2026' (customer not named); a major contract to supply over 40 BRUSH generators for gas-fired utility-scale power plants that will collectively deliver approximately 7 gigawatts and enhance grid resilience in U.S. energy infrastructure; and an integrated power-plus-compression solution award for the Tengiz Gas Separation Complex in Kazakhstan. The BRUSH brand also supplies synchronous condensers for grid inertia and voltage control, and Baker Hughes provides steam turbine generators for small modular reactor projects.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 1 gigawatt NovaLT slot reservation (data center); over 40 BRUSH generators, approximately 7 gigawatts

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center outlook: Baker Hughes now expects to book approximately $3 billion of data center-related orders between 2025 and 2027 (an analyst called this a doubling of the prior 3-year target; management did not dispute it), which the CEO said reflects 'a healthy and growing pipeline'. Framing: 'Resilient power supply has emerged as a key bottleneck', with data center build-out increasing demand for behind-the-meter power; industry estimates put AI infrastructure spending at more than $500 billion in 2025, expected to approach $1 trillion annually in the late 2020s; data center power demand is projected to grow at a 12% compounded annual growth rate through 2040, and global power demand to double to approximately 60,000 terawatt hours by 2040.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $3 billion of data center-related orders between 2025 and 2027; AI infrastructure spending more than $500 billion in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 guidance (CFO, midpoints; excludes the divested PSI business, deconsolidates SPC, and excludes Chart until it closes): company revenue $27.25 billion and adjusted EBITDA $4.85 billion (organic adjusted EBITDA growth in the mid-single digit range), free cash flow conversion approaching 50%; IET orders $13.5 billion to $15.5 billion (flat at the midpoint organically; a fourth consecutive year of at least $13 billion) on LNG, FPSO and gas infrastructure awards and sustained power systems strength; IET revenue $13.5 billion and EBITDA $2.7 billion, reaching the 20% IET margin target; OFSE revenue $13.75 billion and EBITDA $2.475 billion. Q1 2026: revenue $6.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA $1.06 billion, IET EBITDA $600 million, OFSE EBITDA $540 million; IET range drivers include GTE backlog conversion and 'the impact of any supply chain tightness'. Management remains confident in the Horizon Two target of more than $40 billion of IET orders (2026 to 2028) and a 20% company adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $27.25 billion, adjusted EBITDA $4.85 billion; IET orders $13.5 billion to $15.5 billion; IET EBITDA $2.7 billion; Q1 revenue $6.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA $1.06 billion; Horizon Two IET orders more than $40 billion

quarterly_data.signal: New Energy: orders of $434 million in Q4 and a record $2 billion for 2025, well above the $1.4 billion to $1.6 billion target; notable awards include an order to supply the 5 Organic Rankine Cycle power plants at Fervo's Cape Station project, expected to deliver 300 megawatts of power to the grid, with Baker Hughes also providing subsurface expertise. 2026 New Energy order target $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion, with the CEO expecting the trajectory to continue led by CCUS, flex-fuel power and geothermal solutions. The pending Chart acquisition is expected to add thermal-management capabilities and enable integrated trigeneration solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: New Energy orders $434 million (Q4), $2 billion (2025); 2026 target $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion; Fervo 300 megawatts
